schema.description: Business input exposed to the program as the global `POA_INPUT` value. When omitted, the program receives an empty object.

The program this cell runs: a base64-encoded `.poa`, which is a zip with `manifest.toml` at its root, the JavaScript body that manifest names as its entry, and whatever that body needs.

The server runs the body with the MCP servers the manifest declares, and waits for them before the cell starts. A caller with nothing but a snippet of JavaScript sends it the same way, as a package whose manifest declares no servers.

Whether this caller can answer a question the program asks, and therefore whether the program gets an `ask` function at all.

Omitted or null means disabled, which is what every client that predates this field sends and what it has always got. The server does not guess: a caller that can reach a person says so, and one that cannot says that instead of leaving it out.

A path that is guaranteed to be absolute and normalized (though it is not guaranteed to be canonicalized or exist on the filesystem).

InitializeResponse__193ff4d__ServerCapab.description:
Server-declared capabilities returned during initialize.

Every field defaults to `false`, so a server that predates a capability — and therefore omits the whole object — reads as not supporting it. Clients must gate newer request fields on these before sending them; a server that does not understand a field would otherwise accept and silently ignore it, which no error-driven downgrade can detect.

ThreadResumeParams__2a7a571.description:
There are three ways to resume a thread: 1. By thread_id: load the thread from disk by thread_id and resume it. 2. By history: instantiate the thread from memory and resume it. 3. By path: load the thread from disk by path and resume it.

For non-running threads, the precedence is: history > non-empty path > thread_id. If using history or a non-empty path for a non-running thread, the thread_id param will be ignored.

If thread_id identifies a running thread, app-server rejoins that thread and treats a non-empty path as a consistency check against the active rollout path. Empty string path values are treated as absent.

Prefer using thread_id whenever possible.

There are two ways to fork a thread: 1. By thread_id: load the thread from disk by thread_id and fork it into a new thread. 2. By path: load the thread from disk by path and fork it into a new thread.

Prefer using thread_id whenever possible.

package.description:
The program this cell runs: a base64-encoded `.poa`, which is a zip with `manifest.toml` at its root, the JavaScript body that manifest names as its entry, and whatever that body needs.

The server runs the body with the MCP servers the manifest declares, and waits for them before the cell starts. A caller with nothing but a snippet of JavaScript sends it the same way, as a package whose manifest declares no servers.

userInputMode.description:
Whether this caller can answer a question the program asks, and therefore whether the program gets an `ask` function at all.

Omitted or null means disabled, which is what every client that predates this field sends and what it has always got. The server does not guess: a caller that can reach a person says so, and one that cannot says that instead of leaving it out.

ThreadCodeModeExecParams__667fdd3__CodeM.description:
Whether the caller that started a code-mode cell can answer a question, and whether the cell is even allowed to ask one.

The three values are not three ways of asking. `Disabled` says the cell has no asking feature at all, so the `ask` global is never installed; the other two both install it and differ only in whether anyone is listening. That distinction is what lets one script run unchanged in the foreground and the background: backgrounded, `ask` still exists and returns a refusal the script can branch on, rather than blowing up as `ask is not a function`.

oneOf.description:
No `ask` global. Model-driven code-mode execution, and any caller that omits the field.

This is the default because the safe failure of a forgotten field is "cannot ask", never "unexpectedly able to ask".
`ask` is installed and reaches the user. Only the TUI's `/poa fg` selects this.
`ask` is installed but returns non-interactive without contacting anyone. The TUI's `/poa bg` and `brainary exec --poa` select this.

The Anthropic Messages API at `/v1/messages`.

Most vendors do not serve `/v1/responses`, but many serve an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`, so this is the second protocol that buys the widest model coverage.
